newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants more sugar refineries, fewer imports.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants more sugar refineries, fewer imports.

text.p: Russia wants to increase its sugar refining capacity to 3.25 million tonnes by 2000 from 2.10 million tonnes and to reduce refined sugar imports, according to a state programme cited by Interfax news agency on Wednesday.
The agency said the government would examine the proposal on Friday, but did not say how it would be financed.
Russia produces 2.0 million tonnes of refined sugar and imports 1.5 million tonnes of raws for refining and 2.0 million tonnes of refined sugar each year.
Interfax said sugar consumption had declined since the 1991 Soviet collapse. The average Russian consumed 31 kg in 1995, compared to 42 kg in 1990. Figures for 1996 were unavailable.
Imported sugar accounted for 19 kg of per capita consumption last year, up from 14 kg.
Russia's 95 sugar refineries are working far below capacity due to an oversupply of white sugar, mainly from Ukraine. They can process up to 3.5 million tonnes of raws a year.
